claims.text: SemVer 2.0.0: given MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, increment MAJOR for incompatible API changes, MINOR for backward compatible functionality, PATCH for backward compatible bug fixes.
claims.source_hint: semver.org/spec/v2.0.0 Summary and rules 6-8 (also github.com/semver/semver semver.md)

claims.text: SemVer 2.0.0: patch resets to 0 when minor is incremented; patch and minor reset to 0 when major is incremented.
SemVer 2.0.0 rule 2: X, Y, Z are non-negative integers and each element increases numerically, e.g. 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0 -> 1.11.0; precedence compares major, minor, patch numerically.
SemVer 2.0.0 rule 1: software using semantic versioning must declare a public API, in code or documentation.
SemVer 2.0.0 rules 4-5: major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development, anything may change at any time and the public API should not be considered stable; 1.0.0 defines the public API.
SemVer defines a bug fix as an internal change that fixes incorrect behavior; such a fix alone is a PATCH.

At stage-1 the API exposes POST /api/v1/auth/login, GET /api/v1/products(/{id}), POST /api/v1/orders, GET /api/v1/orders/{id}, PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel; its image is donhang-api:stage-1 and no file states an API product version.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1 STAGE.md, docker-compose.yml:86, DonHang.Api/Controllers/*.cs (DonHang.App/pubspec.yaml version is the app's, not the API's)

claims.text: At stage-1 OrderService.CancelOrderAsync still allows cancelling a shipped order (a known gap described in STAGE.md), which the Try it treats as a bug to fix.
Adding /api/v2 next to an unchanged /api/v1 is backward compatible for existing clients (MINOR under SemVer); retiring /api/v1 is a breaking change (MAJOR).
claims.source_hint: semver.org/spec/v2.0.0 rules 7-8 applied; backend.l2.api-versioning (v1 unchanged next to v2)

claims.text: Which part to raise is decided by whoever cuts the release; SemVer is a convention, no tool checks it unless the team adds one.
claims.source_hint: semver.org FAQ (What do I do if I accidentally release a backward incompatible change as a minor version?)

claims.text: Sorting version strings as text puts 1.10.0 before 1.9.0, because '1' < '9' character by character.
claims.source_hint: lexicographic order of strings (e.g. printf '1.9.0\n1.10.0\n' | sort)

claims.text: SemVer 2.0.0 rule 3: once a version is released its contents must not be modified; any modification is released as a new version, so even a change invisible to clients gets a new (PATCH or MINOR) number.
SemVer 2.0.0 rule 8: a major version MAY also include minor and patch level changes, so a release that adds and breaks raises MAJOR; rule 9 defines pre-release labels (not taught).
